card.statement:
Let $A$ be
a square real matrix
such that $A^2$ is
normal. Then $A$ is
orthogonally similar
to a direct sum of
real blocks of the
form

\begin{equation}
\begin{bmatrix} \lambda
\end{bmatrix},\qquad
\tau \begin{bmatrix} 0
& 1\\ \nu&0
\end{bmatrix}\ (|\nu|< 1,
\ \tau >0) ,
\end{equation}

and

\begin{equation}
\begin{bmatrix}
a & -b \\
b&a
\end{bmatrix}\ (b>0),
\quad
\tau\! \begin{bmatrix}
0&0&1&0\\ 0&0&0&1\\
c&-d&0&0 \\
d&c&0&0
\end{bmatrix}
\ (d> 0,\ c^2+d^2<1,\
\tau
>0).
\end{equation}

This direct sum is
uniquely determined by
$A$, up to permutation
of summands. It can be
obtained from the
canonical form of $A$
under unitary
similarity that is a
direct sum of matrices
of the form <<ref:s2>>
by replacing all pairs
of summands

\begin{equation*}
[a+bi]\oplus [a-bi]\
(b>0),\quad
\tau\!\begin{bmatrix}
0 & 1\\ c+di&0
\end{bmatrix}
\oplus\tau\!
\begin{bmatrix} 0 &
1\\ c-di&0
\end{bmatrix}\ (d>0)
\end{equation*}

by the corresponding
matrices <<ref:ca4>>.
Conversely, if $A$ is
unitarily similar to a
direct sum of blocks
of the form
<<ref:ca3>> and
<<ref:ca4>>, then
$A^2$ is normal.
card.label: Theorem 2

paper.title: Classification of squared normal operators on unitary and Euclidean spaces
paper.abstract: We give a canonical form for a complex matrix, whose square is normal, under transformations of unitary similarity as well as a canonical form for a real matrix, whose square is normal, under transformations of orthogonal similarity.
